proved_theorems.ground: extend sets abandonment = not visited(sigma(u)) at the run end and dF = int(abandonment); area_a_prune_reason returns F_exceeded for F>1; F is monotone
proved_theorems.name: Forced rotation length (FRL)
proved_theorems.statement: With F at TARGET_F, the only F-preserving rotation length is ell = m-1, m = min{j>=1 : sigma^j(p) visited}: only the maximal rotation run survives. Branching <= 4.

proved_theorems.name: Phi ledger
proved_theorems.statement: dP=1 and d(visited)=ell+1 per macro edge, so dPhi = ell-5, cost = 5-ell >= 0, Phi non-increasing, Phi(initial)=6, total spend = 6 - Phi(s)

consequences: at most one hexagon has degree 2, none has degree 3
every component of B is an orbit-star except at most one, which is two orbit-stars bridged at a single hexagon
AT MOST ONE unordered E-orbit pair is ever co-component
r is non-decreasing, so once r=1 the co-component pair is frozen and the future cannot change the answer
a length-4 incidence path (the third-component merge) would need r>=2 and is impossible
proved_theorems.name: UNIQUE BRIDGE: 6r <= 11 - Phi hence r <= 1
proved_theorems.statement: r := P - |T| = sum over hexagon nodes of (deg-1). Every hexagon holds at most 6 windows so 6|T| >= visited = 6P + Phi - 11, giving 6r <= 11 - Phi; with Phi>=0, r <= 1.

proved_theorems.name: Orbit-changing lemma over the macro alphabet
proved_theorems.statement: For all 24 macro generators sigma^ell.a and all 720 words, orbit and hexagon both change

proved_theorems.name: LIVE/DEAD incidence (one-sided, partition-free)
proved_theorems.one_sidedness: partial knowledge of the dead set yields a LARGER graph, so separation certificates from partial data stay valid
proved_theorems.statement: visited-but-unregistered permutations can never be registered; dead-ness is monotone; every rotation target is dead at once; B(s') is a subgraph of B_live(s) for every descendant. Orbits separated in B_live(s) are separated forever.

proved_theorems.name: Re-entry cost
proved_theorems.statement: Entering a hexagon holding a>=1 visited windows forces the next macro edge to cost >= a; leaving a hexagon with gaps and returning costs >= 6 in total. With Phi <= 5 no hexagon first entered at or after s can ever be bridged.

proved_theorems.name: sigma-adjacency admissibility lemma
proved_theorems.statement: Two distinct E-orbits sharing a hexagon admit a weight-3 transition iff their ports in it are sigma-adjacent; all such pairs are bidirectional; the same 360 pairs are weight-2-admissible

proved_theorems.name: POST-R1 R-COCOMPONENT OBSTRUCTION (short-root form)
proof_sketch: hub hexagon 0 has positions 1..ell0 DEAD (root rotation targets) and ell0+1..5 free; Phi(root)=ell0+1
r=0 forces b_cur=1, so the gaps outside the current hexagon number 6-Phi and all lie in the hub
a joint into hub position g makes the NEXT macro edge cost exactly g; g<=Phi is required for the bridged state to have any legal successor
free positions start at ell0+1, so the only survivable bridge is g=ell0+1, whose pair is at sigma-distance 2 or 3 for ell0 in {1,2,3} and admits no weight-3 transition (T7)
the one sigma-adjacent live partner sits at position 5 and costs 5 > Phi <= 4, so bridging to it yields a state with ZERO legal macro edges
the other sigma-adjacent partner (position 1) is dead by T5
no second bridge is ever possible by T3
